skills.q: Across every company and project I run, what is actually in my files, what is messy or stale, and what does the topology reveal about how the team really works?
reach: Something is a mess and you want the picture before touching anything (Scan, then Advise)
An external review is coming: run both, Advise for the filesystem and Deliverable Audit for what the documents claim
Generated deliverables have piled up and you cannot remember which one answers which question
A new company needs its working structure laid down (Onboarding), or the convention behind it written once (Standardize)
You want to know what the file topology says about the real team boundaries before anyone designs an org (Architect)

nf.w: building or curating the data room
correcting a stale claim or merging two overlapping documents
nf.o: the Founder-OS skill that produced them

gives: Scan: a structured inventory (tree shape, hotspots, duplicate groups proven by hash) plus a metadata-only scan index cached under _snapshots/
Advise: two artifacts, always both, a prioritized human report and a replayable dry-run action plan
Deliverable Audit: one prioritized report of measured overlap, missing boundary blocks, stale pointers, manifest gaps and expired time-bound claims
File-Organization-Standard.md, versioned, with its path referenced back into config
Architect: the inferred de-facto functional map, the target information architecture, a prioritized friction list and the handoff notes
skills.rule: Anything measurable is measured, never asserted. Duplicates are proven by SHA-256 after a name, size and mtime prefilter; document overlap is reported as a figure over shared headings and key terms, with two or more major sections in common as the merge threshold; manifest completeness is reported per item rather than as one aggregate claim.

skills.q: What teams, roles, reporting lines and hires should this company have, and how does the change get rolled out?
reach: There is no target org written down and how should I structure my team needs an answer with a rationale (Org Design)
The team feels slow or siloed and the friction is in the interfaces rather than the boxes (Team Ops and Performance)
You need to know whether to hire at all, and who next (Workforce Planning), then the JD, scorecard and loop (Hiring Prep)
A reorg needs phasing, sequencing, communicating and measuring (Org Rollout)
Architect handed you a friction list with team-structure implications: a function carrying too much, a missing role, a team that should split

nf.w: the personnel decision itself, and pay

gives: Organization-Model.md, the only named file and the contract with workspace-ops
The target org across four dimensions, the model rationale with its citations and stated trade-off, transition notes, and the RACI
Interaction modes and cross-team operations written as workflows: intake form, lead-times, dependency-resolution steps, escalation ladder
A prioritized workforce plan: each gap, the recommended option, its reasoning, sequence position and cost implication
Hiring Prep: role definition, job description, scorecard, interview plan, candidate prospectus
Org Rollout: the phased roadmap and a metrics table with a baseline and a target window per metric
skills.rule: Every role is defined by its negative space. Accountability, responsibilities, decision rights, and an explicit not responsible for, with exactly one Accountable per decision in the RACI. Negative space prevents overlap better than long responsibility lists.

skills.q: How do I keep one honest, examiner-ready room for this company, find and reach the investors who actually fit, and hand each outside party exactly what they should see?
reach: A company needs its canonical data room laid down for the first time (Bootstrap), or the latest deliverables picked up into it (Sync)
You want to know what is missing before anyone else asks (Audit, the safe default when a request is ambiguous)
A raise is starting: build the list, score fit, run cold and warm outreach, track the pipeline (Family 2)
A named examiner has arrived: an investor, a competition or grant call, a DD questionnaire, the board, an auditor, an acquirer (Family 3)

nf.w: producing strategy, decks, financials or metrics from scratch
authoring the board pack or the investor letter
a formal compliance opinion or contract review

gives: Bootstrap: the room on your platform, from dataroom.canonical_structure, sector overlays applied, idempotent on re-run
Sync: the room updated in place, everything indexed by reference, only approved finals copied, each stamped audience, lens, version, source_skill, sensitivity
Audit: a punch list of blocker, should-fix and nice-to-have, naming the yardstick it graded against
One living investor tracker, a ranked shortlist with a one-line reason each, and the pipeline in outreach.crm_location
Fundraise Prep: the access-filtered investor view, an opened access-log entry, and a readiness summary phrased as seed-ready except N items
DD Support: the Q&A tracker statused answered, partial, missing or N/A, plus the evidence tracker behind it
Audit Prep: the evidence index, the gap flags, and a readiness percentage per control area
skills.rule: Completeness is only ever relative to a named checklist, and the checklist is selected at runtime from the company's jurisdiction. There is no hardcoded default, and every readiness claim and package footer states standard applied: <name>. Grading a founder against another market's list makes them look unprepared to the investors they actually have.

gloss.d: The only places workspace-ops may look, and in v1.1 reorganize. It never wanders outside them, and never follows a symlink that leads out.
The absolute boundary, loaded and checked before every operation. Missing or malformed and the skill stops and asks: it will not guess a safety boundary.
Where a superseded file goes instead of being deleted, at _archive/<timestamp>/<original relative path>. Append-only from the skill's side.
The listing of every file a batch will touch, written before it runs. It is what makes a reversal provable rather than hopeful.
Per batch, the reverse operation for every move. One command derived from it reverses the whole batch.
The machine-readable action plan Advise emits. Its only verbs are move and archive; each entry carries source, destination, reason, provider and its reverse.
What stops the report being the same report every time. Declined findings are suppressed, applied ones skipped, deferred ones resurface.
Same name and different content, or high similarity. Flagged for human judgment, never auto-merged.
Content-level, not file-level. It looks inside the documents at what they claim and whether they still agree with each other.
The opening line of a narrative document saying this answers X, for Y see Z. Its absence is what lets the overlap happen in the first place.
Produced artifacts and tabs checked against the Minimum Output Manifest the producing skill declared. Reported per item, never as one aggregate claim.
A reference to a file that has been moved, renamed or archived. Archiving one file and leaving three documents pointing at its old path is the commonest form of quiet rot.
How information is structured so it mirrors the company's real functional, product and team shape. Architect owns this and stops here.
The org chart the files reveal rather than the one the company claims. Stated as a hypothesis grounded in named evidence, with confidence marked.
The portable convention derived from the patterns you already use well, plus best practice where they are thin. Versioned, and applied by Onboarding and Advise.
The single description of how the company is organized: entities, units, products, sites, work modes, roles, reporting lines, rituals, RACI. The contract between the two skills.
The structural pattern chosen by fit, not by fashion: stage, product architecture, team size and work flow matched to a model or hybrid, with the principle cited and the trade-off stated.
How many layers the current size warrants. The same model renders differently at 20, 80 and 400 people.
A manager leads roughly 5 to 9 direct reports well; beyond about 15 to 20 a layer is added or the unit splits. The single most useful trigger for adding a layer.
How much a team can hold well. When a team is a bottleneck, ask whether its load is too high before asking whether its people are the problem.
How two teams work together: collaboration (high bandwidth, keep it temporary), X-as-a-service (the default for stable interfaces), facilitating (help, then step away).
The explicit non-ownership line on every role. Negative space prevents overlap better than a long responsibility list.
Key decisions by role, with exactly one Accountable per decision. Carried in the Organization Model.
Each gap, the recommended option, the reasoning, its position in the sequence, and its cost or runway implication.
The five options weighed on every gap before a hire is recommended: build, hire, reassign, outsource, defer, each with cost and time-to-impact.
The few outcomes and competencies that predict success in a role, each with what good looks like. It is what interviewers score against, so signal beats vibes.
The brief sent to candidates: company, mission, the role's real impact, the team, stage, comp framing, first-year success. Honest about challenges, not hype.
When the inferred de-facto map diverges from the Organization Model. The model wins, and the divergence is flagged back as evidence rather than silently overridden.
The jurisdiction-neutral folder set, from 00_Overview to 09_Traction_&_Metrics plus 99_DD_QA_&_Trackers. Deliberately a superset, and stable, never re-derived.
Additive folders and checklist items applied by company_type. Extends the base, never replaces it.
Five fields on every synced item: audience, lens, version, source_skill, sensitivity.
What may be shown to whom. restricted means principals and counsel only, and is hard-blocked from every package by default.
Sync indexes everything by reference and copies only approved finals. It is what keeps the room from becoming a second, drifting copy of your workspace.
How an item with no local equivalent is marked, with a one-line reason. Nobody chases a document their investors will never ask for, and it is not carried as a gap.
Read the jurisdiction, apply the mapped reference body if one is known, otherwise research the national association at runtime and cite it. Unset or cross-border: say so and ask once.
Which folder subset and depth a given raise needs. Stage drives depth; jurisdiction drives which named standard applies.
Stage 25, sector 20, check size 15, geography 10, portfolio fit 10, value-add 10, warm path 10, tuned per raise. Output is a ranked shortlist with a one-line reason each.
Warm before cold, always: the recommended intro path is the named route where one exists. Cold sends are capped by outreach.daily_send_cap, and every touch is logged.
Researched, Contacted, Replied, Meeting, Diligence, Term Sheet, Closed or Passed. The snapshot is count by stage, this week's actions, stale contacts to nudge.
Nurture for investors who have not invested. Updates to those who have are Board and Investor Delivery, which is examination-grade reporting. Easy to get backwards.
A received legal, financial, tech or commercial question set. Each question maps to evidence in the room and is statused answered, partial, missing or N/A.
Authored by Founder-OS narrative-assets-ops. investor-ops delivers it: files it, audience-gates it, logs the distribution, manages the cadence, and routes back upstream when it is missing or stale.
Who was granted access, to what, at what sensitivity, and when. Non-negotiable in a live process.
Evidence assembled per control area for an audit framework. Like every readiness claim, it names the framework it was measured against.
There is no deletion path, in any mode, in any version. A file that must leave its place is moved to the timestamped archive.
An unreachable path, platform or linked repo is reported, not fatal. The one exception is a missing safety boundary in workspace-ops, which stops and asks.
Investor facts are cited or flagged unknown, affordability is checked against real financials or left alone, and a model built without evidence is labelled as such.

gloss.t: No em dash, no bare URLs
gloss.d: In every mode of every skill, in every output. Verbatim quoted source text is the only exception, and every link is embedded in descriptive text.

miss.t: My files are a mess across companies
miss.j: You want the picture before you touch anything, and you want to know what the documents still claim.

chain.h: read-only inventory: tree shape, hotspots, duplicate groups proven by hash, plus a metadata-only index cached under _snapshots/ so the next run only processes what changed
the prioritized report and the replayable dry-run plan: consolidations, orphans, naming, duplicates, stale items, misfiles, each with source, destination, reason and reverse
inside the documents: measured overlap, missing boundary blocks, stale pointers, manifest gaps, expired deadlines and prices, duplicate formats, cloud-sync artifacts, page density
writes File-Organization-Standard.md from the patterns you already use well, so Onboarding and Advise apply one convention across every company

rules.h: Advise and Deliverable Audit are not the same check
rules.b: Advise looks at the filesystem. Deliverable Audit looks inside the documents at what they claim and whether they still agree. A workspace can be perfectly tidy and still hold two documents answering the same question, a pointer to a file archived last month, and a deadline that has passed. Run both before any external review.

rules.h: Nothing is ever deleted
rules.b: A file that must leave its place is moved under a timestamped archive with its relative path preserved. There is no code path that calls rm or empties a trash, in any version. If you truly want something gone, you delete it from the archive yourself.

rules.h: The advice already is the executable artifact
rules.b: The plan's only verbs are move and archive, and each operation carries its own reverse. v1.1 Execute replays it one to one with no re-deciding at apply time, which is why the plan seeds the undo log rather than being rebuilt from scratch.

rules.h: Source material is excluded from the audit entirely
rules.b: Generated content can be regenerated and source cannot. Judging co-founder notes, transcripts and third-party papers by the same rules is how a founder loses a transcript.

rules.h: A declined finding does not come back
rules.b: The decisions register suppresses what you already declined, skips what was applied, and resurfaces what you deferred. A finding that reappears because the file itself changed is treated as new, which is the only case where repeating it is useful.

ex.t: Three companies in one Documents folder, and a review in two weeks
s: First
Set workspace_ops.scope_paths and workspace_ops.never_touch. Without the second the skill stops and asks, which is the correct behaviour rather than a bug.
Scan
The inventory and the duplicate groups, proven by SHA-256 after a name, size and mtime prefilter. Near-duplicates come out on a separate list.
Advise
The report to read and the plan to keep. Nothing on disk has changed.
Deliverable Audit
Run it before the review, not after: this is where the pointer to last month's archived file and the deadline that already passed surface.
Architect
Only if the question has become what does this say about how we work. It maps information, then hands the people question to functional-hr-ops.

br: Asking for a clean-up and expecting files to move. In v1.0, Scan and Advise change nothing and Onboarding only creates new folders in an empty target.
Auto-merging a near-duplicate. Same name and different content is a human judgment, never an automatic action.
Comparing two documents without normalizing encoding first. Arrows, escaped ampersands and smart quotes produce false alarms, and a check that cries wolf gets ignored.

miss.j: You want a target org with a rationale, not a chart drawn from fashion.

chain.h: the de-facto functional map plus the prioritized friction list: silos, cross-team duplication, ownerless areas, single-person bottlenecks, access mismatches
the operating model chosen by fit, the scale tier, four dimensions (functional, product, geographic, work mode), roles with their non-ownership, the RACI, and Organization-Model.md
interaction modes per boundary, cross-team operations written as workflows with intake, lead-times and an escalation ladder, then the friction diagnosis and its levers
pilot, then scale, then optimize, sequenced by dependency, with a metrics table carrying a baseline and a target window per metric
reads Organization-Model.md back and mirrors it in information architecture, so files land where the org says they belong

rules.h: Evidence first, then design
rules.b: Start from the map Architect inferred, not an idealized chart. If it is absent the skill will offer to run Scan plus Architect, or proceed from what you tell it and label the model as not yet evidence-grounded, which is the honest outcome rather than a blocked one.

rules.h: Fit over fashion, with the trade-off stated
rules.b: No operating model is correct in the abstract. Stage, product architecture, team size and work flow pick the model or hybrid, the structural principle is cited (Dunbar, two-pizza, Conway, Tuckman, span of control), and the cost of the choice is written down. default_operating_model left blank means choose by fit, and there is no house default.

rules.h: Scale by splitting, never by front-loading
rules.b: Add a business unit or department only when span of control passes roughly 15 to 20 reports or cognitive load clearly demands it. A one-team business unit is the classic tell: a bureaucracy layer with no job.

rules.h: Most friction is in the interfaces, not the boxes
rules.b: Every pair of teams that must work together gets a named interaction mode: collaboration for genuine discovery and kept temporary, X-as-a-service as the default for stable relationships, facilitating to inject a capability then step away. Permanent collaboration signals a wrong boundary.

rules.h: The model beats the inferred map
rules.b: Where the two diverge, workspace-ops flags the drift back rather than silently overriding the model. Either the org changed or the model is stale, and both are worth knowing.

br: Designing the org before anyone has looked at how the work actually flows. You will produce a chart that describes a company that does not exist.
Tying a friction to a person. Frictions are tied to a structural or operational cause, always.
Deciding the reorg here. This skill recommends, drafts and sequences; hire, fire, reorg and compensation calls are yours, and personnel-sensitive steps are flagged for you and for counsel.

miss.t: Decide whether to hire, and who
miss.j: The question is not who to hire. It is whether this gap is real and whether hiring is the right answer to it.

chain.h: gap analysis against the target model, honest need detection, the five options weighed per gap, then sequencing against stage, runway and dependency
role definition, job description, scorecard, interview plan and candidate prospectus, for the role you confirmed

rules.h: A need is a scoped gap, not a feeling
rules.b: We are busy is not a need. No one owns billing and three deals are stalled on it is. State the work each gap unblocks and the cost of leaving it open.

rules.h: Never jump straight to hire
rules.b: Every gap is weighed across build, hire, reassign, outsource, defer, each with its trade-off, rough cost and time-to-impact. Build is cheapest culturally and slower, and needs slack you may not have.

rules.h: Sequence by dependency, and flag affordability
rules.b: A manager before their reports, a platform capability before the teams that depend on it, revenue-unblocking before nice-to-have. Affordability is checked against the financials where they are known and flagged, never invented.

rules.h: The scorecard is what interviewers score against
rules.b: The few outcomes and competencies that actually predict success, each with what good looks like, and an interview loop mapped to them so each competency is covered once, well. Signal beats vibes, and redundant stages produce neither.

rules.h: It frames the band, it does not set pay
rules.b: The job description marks where you set the numbers. Employment-law specifics leave the repo, to a legal skill or counsel.

br: A job description that is a task list. Lead with mission and outcomes, keep must-haves few and real, and write it to deter the wrong person as plainly as it attracts the right one.
Hiring into a structure nobody has written down. Without the model there is nothing to measure the gap against.

miss.j: One canonical, examiner-ready room per company, kept honest between raises rather than assembled during one.

chain.h: optional but worth it first: a clean substrate makes Sync classification reliable, and Onboarding deliberately leaves the data room seam rather than recreating those folders

the room on dataroom.platform, named per company, from dataroom.canonical_structure, sector overlays by company_type, a seeded root index, and 99_DD_QA_&_Trackers with empty Q&A and access-log placeholders

picks up the Founder-OS deliverables, classifies each to a folder and a lens, indexes everything by reference, copies only approved finals, stamps the metadata, versions and archives what it supersedes
read-only. Names the yardstick, then returns gaps, stale items, version conflicts, near-duplicates and sensitivity-tag issues as a blocker, should-fix and nice-to-have punch list

rules.h: Index everything, copy the finals, stamp the metadata
rules.b: The hybrid is deliberate. Indexing by reference and copying only approved finals is what keeps the room from becoming a second, drifting copy of your workspace. Every copied item carries audience, lens, version, source_skill and sensitivity.

rules.h: Bootstrap is idempotent
rules.b: Re-running fills gaps without clobbering, so there is no reason to avoid it when you are unsure. And it does not invent folders: the taxonomy comes from config.

rules.h: The taxonomy is stable; what goes in it is not
rules.b: The folder set, the numbering, the meaning of each folder and the sector overlays are never re-derived. What is re-derived per jurisdiction: which documents are expected at each stage, the corporate-form documents, employment and IP-assignment norms, and the regulatory and privacy annexes.

rules.h: One company per run, isolated
rules.b: Each company gets its own room, pipeline and packages. Two are never merged, and one company's data never appears inside another's.

rules.h: Superseded is archived, not deleted
rules.b: Latest version in place, history in the timestamped archive. Near-duplicates are reported for human judgment rather than merged.

br: Building the room by hand alongside Sync. You now have two rooms and no way to say which is current.
Treating the Swiss worked example as the standard. It is one instantiation of a jurisdiction-neutral taxonomy, and the applied standard is selected per run.
Leaving items untagged for sensitivity. The gate in Family 3 has nothing to work with, and the first package leaks or blocks everything.

miss.j: Build the target list, score fit, run outreach, and track the whole raise as a pipeline.

chain.h: one living tracker from outreach.sources, warm network first: type, stage and sector focus, geography, check size, thesis, portfolio and conflicts, warm path, source, status
ranked by outreach.fit_weights, which sum to 100, with a one-line reason per investor and the recommended intro path
drafted sends and follow-ups on the configured cadence, materials referenced from Founder-OS, the pipeline moved through outreach.pipeline_stages, every touch logged
short, honest nurture for the warm-but-not-closed: traction since last touch, momentum, round status

rules.h: Never fabricate an investor fact
rules.b: Thesis, check size and portfolio are researched from real, citable sources. Unknown fields are marked unknown rather than guessed, because the guess is what gets quoted back to you in the meeting.

rules.h: Warm before cold, every time
rules.b: Warm path strength is one of the seven scoring weights, and the recommended intro path names the route where one exists. Cold sends are capped by outreach.daily_send_cap.

rules.h: The materials come from Founder-OS
rules.b: The teaser, deck and one-pager are pulled from narrative-assets-ops and referenced, not rewritten here. A second version of the deck written for one email is how the story starts drifting.

rules.h: Prospect update is not board delivery
rules.b: Nurture for investors who have not invested is Family 2. Reporting to investors who have is Family 3, and it is examination-grade. This one is easy to get backwards.

br: Scoring a list you assembled from memory. The tracker exists so that every row can name where it came from.
Running outreach before the room is auditable. The first interested investor asks for the room, and Audit takes minutes while assembling it under pressure takes a week.

miss.t: Survive a due diligence or an audit
miss.j: A named examiner has arrived, and everything they see has to be gated, proven against a named checklist, and logged.

chain.h: run this first: it is the single source of truth on gaps, and Fundraise Prep consumes it rather than recomputing them
stage drives the depth, jurisdiction drives the standard. The access-filtered investor view, an optional export bundle, an opened access-log entry, and a readiness summary
ingest the received questionnaire, map every question to evidence in the room, status it, draft answers grounded only in room evidence, gate and log every disclosure
files the pack narrative-assets-ops authored, audience-gates it, logs distribution and manages the cadence. It never authors or re-derives content
name the framework and the privacy regime that actually applies, map controls to evidence, deliver the index, the gap flags and a readiness percentage per control area

rules.h: Completeness is only ever relative to a named checklist
rules.b: Never ready in the abstract. The stage and the standard are stated together in every readiness claim and every package footer as standard applied: <name>. If the jurisdiction is unset or the round is cross-border, the skill says so and asks once rather than picking silently.

rules.h: Restricted is hard-blocked by default
rules.b: Employee PII, litigation, key IP: principals and counsel only. Nothing tagged restricted enters a package or an investor share automatically, and including one takes an explicit per-item override with a logged reason.

rules.h: Every disclosure is logged
rules.b: Who was granted access, to what, at what sensitivity, and when. The access log is non-negotiable in a live process, and it is the thing you cannot reconstruct afterwards.

rules.h: A competition or a grant is a different examiner
rules.b: Not a lighter Fundraise Prep. A jury gets one self-contained document plus named annexes, at a hard deadline, scored against a published weighted rubric and compared with the other submissions. So eligibility is checked before a word is written, the rubric is retrieved at runtime with an absolute date because forms change between cycles, sections are ordered to the criteria in the programme's own vocabulary, and every mandated annex is assembled: a missing one is usually a formal rejection rather than a lost point.

rules.h: Family 3 writes in one place only
rules.b: Everything it produces goes into 99_DD_QA_&_Trackers. It never edits a source file, and a missing item is routed upstream rather than filled in.

ex.t: A term sheet is close and the DD questionnaire has landed
s: Before replying
Audit. It names the yardstick and returns the punch list. Fundraise Prep will consume this and will not recompute it.
Package
Fundraise Prep: gate by sensitivity, build the access-filtered view, open the access-log entry, and state readiness as seed-ready except N items.
Answer
DD Support: each question mapped to a folder, item and version, so the answer is reproducible and a later sync can flag it as stale.
If an item is restricted
It does not travel. Overriding takes an explicit per-item decision with a logged reason.
After the round
Updates to the new investor are Board and Investor Delivery, not Prospect Updates. The rejection letter, where there is one, is filed next to the submission: it names the criteria you failed.

br: Claiming readiness without naming the checklist. It is the one claim an examiner can test in a sentence.
Grading yourself against another market's list. A US seed fund, a UK EIS angel and a Swiss angel club ask for different documents, and preparing to the wrong one reads as unprepared.
Chasing an item with no local equivalent. Mark it n/a (jurisdiction) with a one-line reason and move on.

readers.q: Does this answer our criteria, in our vocabulary, with every annex?

add.q: who owns the coordination between these teams?

add.w: a matrix really applies: a vertical delivery line and a horizontal craft line
add.q: who sets the craft standard, and who sets this quarter's priority?

add.w: several teams rebuild the same undifferentiated work, or one team is a permanent bottleneck
add.q: what can we build once and serve to everyone?

add.w: the company runs more than one entity
add.q: which entity does this unit sit under?

add.q: what did I already decline, and what changed since?

add.w: the scope is large and you re-scan on a cadence
add.q: what actually changed since last time?

add.w: preferences.visual_artifact allows it and someone outside the work has to read it
add.q: can this be one picture instead of three pages?

add.w: reporting or outreach becomes a cadence rather than a one-off
add.q: what goes out this month without me remembering?

breaks.b: If the blacklist or the scope is missing or malformed, the correct behaviour is to stop and ask. Every other failure in this repo is recoverable; reading somewhere it should never have read is not.
The data room is ready means nothing without a stage and a named standard. It is also the one claim an examiner can test in a single question.
The taxonomy is universal, the expectations inside it are not. Preparing to the wrong market's list makes a founder look unprepared to the investors they actually have.

breaks.h: Letting the room become a second workspace
breaks.b: Sync indexes by reference and copies only approved finals for exactly this reason. Copy everything and you now maintain two trees that disagree by the second month.
Departments and business units created before the headcount needs them produce bureaucracy with no job, slow decisions and invented management roles. A one-team business unit is the classic tell.

Deliverable Audit reports and proposes, never rewrites. Correcting a stale claim or merging two overlapping documents belongs to the Founder-OS skill that produced them, or the fix outruns the source.

breaks.h: Fabricating a fact to fill a field
breaks.b: An unsourced investor thesis, an estimated salary, an org model presented as evidence-grounded when no evidence was read. Each is checkable, and each is checked at the worst possible moment.

lean: Fill in .exec-os-config.yml first. Scope and blacklist, the jurisdiction, the linked Founder-OS repos, the target company. All three skills read it before doing anything, and one of them refuses to start without its safety boundary.
Run Scan, then Advise, before you touch anything. Nothing changes on disk, and you get both the report and the plan that v1.1 will replay.

Write the Organization Model even if it is one page. Units with what they own, roles with an explicit not responsible for, and one Accountable per decision. It is the contract the file placement is derived from.
Bootstrap the room once, then let Sync keep it current. Bootstrap is idempotent, so re-running is safe when you are unsure.
Run Audit before you package for anyone. It names the yardstick, and Fundraise Prep consumes its punch list rather than recomputing gaps.
Tag sensitivity on everything, and open the access log the day a live process starts. Both are cheap in advance and impossible to reconstruct afterwards.
rollups: DATA ROOM READINESS against a named stage profile plus the jurisdiction's standard seed-ready except N items the punch list, counted ← never "ready" in the abstract standard applied: <name> stated in every claim and every package footer n/a (jurisdiction) no local equivalent, one-line reason, not carried as a gap DD QUESTION STATUS per question in the tracker answered · partial · missing · N/A ← per item, never one aggregate claim AUDIT READINESS evidence assembled per control area, framework named DOCUMENT OVERLAP measured over shared headings and key terms merge proposed two or more major sections in common ← a figure, not an impression DUPLICATES proven by SHA-256 after a name, size and mtime prefilter near-duplicate flagged for human judgment, never auto-merged PIPELINE count by stage · this week's actions · stale contacts to nudge

standards.w: Read first by all three skills, preferring .exec-os-config.local.yml where it exists. Each reads a different slice, and nothing in here is asked of you twice.
k: workspace_ops.scope_paths
the only places workspace-ops may look, and in v1.1 reorganize
workspace_ops.never_touch
the absolute blacklist, checked before every operation. Missing or malformed and the skill stops and asks
functional_hr_ops.organization_model_path
where Organization-Model.md lives, which is how workspace-ops finds it
default_operating_model
left blank means choose by fit. There is no house default
diligence.default_jurisdiction
read it: there is no built-in default, and the jurisdiction selects the reference standard
dataroom.canonical_structure
the folder taxonomy Bootstrap lays down. It does not invent folders
dataroom.metadata_schema
audience, lens, version, source_skill, sensitivity, stamped on every synced item
outreach.fit_weights
the seven scoring weights, summing to 100, tuned per raise
outreach.daily_send_cap
the anti-spam guardrail: maximum new cold contacts per day
linked_founder_os_repos
the company repos Sync reads and outreach pulls its materials from

standards.w: Not now, not in v1.1, not ever, and the same rule binds investor-ops. A file that must leave its place is moved to a timestamped archive, never trashed. If you truly want it gone, you delete it from the archive yourself.
k: there is no deletion path: not rm, not unlink, not empty trash, not permanently remove
the blacklist is absolute and loaded before any read. Missing or unreadable: stop and ask
stay inside scope. A symlink or mount leading outside is reported, not traversed
archive, not trash: _archive/<timestamp>/<original relative path>, append-only
snapshot before any action, so a reversal is provable rather than hopeful
an undo log per batch, seeded by the reverse operation the Advise plan already carries
confirmation above confirm_batch_over, and a yes applies to the shown plan only
dry-run first, always. There is no path that skips it

standards.w: An unreachable path, platform or linked repo is reported, not fatal: the run continues with what it can reach and states exactly what it could not. One source being offline never fails the whole run. The single exception is a missing or malformed safety boundary in workspace-ops, which stops and asks rather than guessing.

standards.n: No em dash, no bare URLs
standards.w: In every mode of every skill, in every output. Use a comma, a colon, parentheses, or split the sentence. The only exception is verbatim quoted source text. Every link is embedded in descriptive text rather than pasted raw.
The rule that separates a useful answer from one that gets checked and fails. Where a fact is not known, it is marked unknown; where evidence is absent, the output says so.
k: investor data
thesis, check size and portfolio cited from real sources; unknown fields marked unknown rather than guessed
affordability
flagged against known financials, never estimated into existence
the org model
with no Architect evidence it proceeds and labels itself not yet evidence-grounded, which is honest rather than blocked
readiness
always standard applied: <name>, with the stage and jurisdiction named
measurement
duplicates proven by hash, overlap reported as a figure, manifest completeness per item

title: Exec OS: how to use it
sub: Organised by the job you are doing, not by the skill. Three skills, one config, and four rules that cut across every mode of every one of them. Each job shows which skill to run in what order, what it hands to the next, the rules that make it work, and what breaks it. For everything about one skill, open its SKILL.md; for what it will do before you run it, open HANDBOOK.md. This page is how the three fit together.
footer: Exec OS · everything about one skill lives in its SKILL.md · what a skill needs and returns is in HANDBOOK.md · why each rule exists is in CHANGELOG.md · generated by scripts/explorer/build.py, do not edit by hand

model.h: What every skill here does, whatever it is about

model.lede: One owner per object. A skill needing something it does not own reads the identifier and attaches to it, rather than minting a second one for the same thing.

model.h: Anything describing a set of records is computed
model.lede: A field describing other records diverges within a week when typed by hand, and a hand-filled rollup is noise that looks like signal — worse than an empty field, because nobody knows it is wrong.
Different people arrive with different questions. Nobody should have to read a document written for someone else.
Not a beginner mode. This is what stays true at every size; everything else is an addition a specific question makes necessary.

model.h: What to add, and what triggers it
model.lede: Add a field when the question is asked, not in anticipation. And remove one that stopped being read.

model.h: The same model in any environment
model.lede: The mechanism changes, the rule does not. Pick the one your team already opens — a model living in a tool nobody maintains is dead on arrival.

gloss_lede: Every term this suite uses, in one line, grouped by where it lives. The words are not interchangeable — most confusion comes from treating two of them as the same object.
